steps.visual_purpose: Make aligned reference and production summaries visible: category definitions, counts, each window's total and proportions, plus fixed numerical bin edges, eligible counts, means and standard deviations with the specified divisor. Display production-window and reference identifiers alongside the summaries.

Make three evidence categories visible side by side: input distribution P(X) relative to a reference, conditional target relationship P(Y|X), and prediction errors measured using matched ground-truth labels against a declared quality reference. Mark that a change in one category does not establish changes in the others, and that absent matched labels leave labeled quality unresolved.

Make reference and current numeric summaries, eligible totals and aligned category probabilities visible side by side, with the supplied equation, resolved distance, criterion and feature-level verdict. Keep the distribution verdict visibly separate from any claim about prediction quality.

Make the prediction-ID dictionary and retained timestamps visible alongside join eligibility decisions, the 100-ID eligible denominator, the 60-ID mature matched subset, and the separately calculated maturity, error proportion and loss summaries.

Make the baseline statistics, applied threshold/window rule, resolved YAML indicator/owner/response fields, and normal, boundary and breached replay results visible together, including assertion outcomes and emitted owner/action records.

Make the release/telemetry timeline and active-versus-approved identities visible alongside schema, distribution and mature-label evidence. Show each release/cohort's matched eligible-label count, labeled error count and conditional error rate separately, with the tested hypothesis and supported response linked to the relevant evidence.

Make the existing pipeline visible with event-to-entry mappings, identity and investigation checks, intended dataset references, and annotated data-quality/test, training, evaluation and separately authorized promotion stages. Show one eligible-event path and mark the precise downstream stages blocked by a failed required check.

Make the accepted and rejected event paths visible alongside actual stage results: trigger authorization, approved object generation, fatal gate dependencies, retraining execution ARN and consumed snapshot identity. Show step-scoped Secret Manager references and non-disclosure check results without exposing credential values.

steps.visual_purpose: Expose the supplied fixture state after concurrent admissions, reservation, launch, restart recovery and terminal completion: run key, pipeline identity, admission status, persisted job ID, active-slot ownership, terminal confirmation and logical job count. Make same-key identity reuse, different-key exclusion and completed-key retention visible.
Make the function's intermediate conditional rates, expected costs, separately named gate results and final identity-bound verdict visible alongside passing, boundary and failing assertion results.

Make the authorized instance identity, lifecycle state, process/service fault evidence and hypothesis-test result visible before recovery, then show the same instance running with restored service state, readiness and bounded prediction results afterward. Keep credentials out of the displayed evidence.

Make telemetry alignment visible through timestamp, instance identity, process identity, instance state, running-process evidence, CPU percent, memory value and units, and inclusion status. Distinguish matched active-workload rows from stopped or unrelated rows, with separate CPU and memory summaries showing the shared interval, counts, means and standard deviations.

Make workload identities, reporting windows, separate lifecycle windows, charge categories, direct and shared allocations, and explicitly unallocated amounts visible together. Include per-window totals, mean, standard deviation, attribution flags, and a reconciliation total beside the eligible billing-export total.

Make the validated budget/event configuration, below-threshold and breach outcomes, and approved instance identity and status before and after the safe stop visible alongside credential-safe notification and response records.

Make the approved inventory and actual runtime evidence visible before cleanup: container ownership/release labels, running/exit state, relevant logs, compute identity/status and artifact references. After cleanup, show the approved retired resources absent while the active release, required artifacts and bounded readiness/prediction results remain intact. Exclude secret values and sensitive log content.
